Risk: credit assignment failure in delayed reward reinforcement learning
Problem analysis: bias in temporal difference learning and high variance in Monte Carlo learning in delayed reward MDPs
Theoretical insight: eliminating expected future rewards simplifies Q-value estimation to immediate reward mean
Design rationale: reward redistribution achieving zero expected future rewards in SDPs
Implementation mechanism: second-order Markov reward redistribution using differences of consecutive Q-values
Validation evidence: RUDDER speed-up over TD, MC, and MCTS on artificial delayed-reward tasks
Implementation mechanism: LSTM-based return prediction with contribution analysis (RUDDER implementation)
Validation evidence: RUDDER improves PPO performance on delayed-reward Atari games
Intervention: integrate RUDDER reward redistribution during RL fine-tuning to mitigate delayed reward credit assignment
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1806.07857
